QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_3

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is counsel to 'Ganga Infra Trust AIF', a Category I AIF launching its third scheme. The sponsor asks whether a fresh Investment Management Agreement must be signed for each new scheme. What is the correct position?

answer.text: A fresh IMA must be signed for each scheme along with filing with SEBI 30 days prior.
The IMA is signed once for the trust as a whole and is not signed again at the launch of each scheme.
The IMA must be renewed every financial year through an addendum filed with the merchant banker.
The IMA is signed only for the first scheme and a Memorandum of Understanding suffices for subsequent schemes.

explanation.text: The Logic: The IMA is entered into between the trustee (on behalf of the AIF) and the investment manager ONCE at the trust level, and governs the delegation of management powers for the AIF as a whole. It is not re-signed at the launch of each scheme — each new scheme only requires PPM filing through a merchant banker. The Trap: The '30 days prior' and merchant-banker concept belong to PPM filing, not the IMA. No annual renewal or MoU substitute is recognised under the AIF Regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests IMA frequency across all three categories. XIX-A Distributor typically asks only whether the IMA exists, not its re-execution cadence. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating the master IMA, build in a 'scheme extension schedule' template so each new scheme can be on-boarded by a short schedule rather than reopening the whole agreement — saves months of re-negotiation with the trustee for every scheme.
